indications.description: Adult patients with symptomatic metastatic basal cell carcinoma.
Adult patients with locally advanced basal cell carcinoma inappropriate for surgery or radiotherapy.

treatment.schedule_summary: Vismodegib 150 mg orally once daily continuously, with or without food. Four-weekly review is not a planned treatment break. Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity; reassess benefit regularly.
treatment.duration_text: Continuous daily treatment until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with regular benefit/tolerance review.
administration_instructions: Swallow the capsule whole with 200 mLwater; do not open, crush or chew. Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
If a dose is missed, skip it and resume the next scheduled dose; do not double up.
The NCCP/EMA documents reviewed do not supply a specific vomited-dose replacement rule. Contact the team before taking an extra dose.
NCCP specifies no recommended dose reductions. Trial interruptions of up to 4 weeks are contextual evidence, not permission to self-pause or a mandatory permanent-stop deadline.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: NCCP00236v3p3: oral minimal-to-low emetogenic potential; refer to local policy. Premedications not usually required.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
other_supportive_care: No routine premedication is usually required; agree symptom/rescue antiemetic support with the local team.
All patients need Pregnancy Prevention Programme counselling, relevant precautions and the official patient materials.

WCBP: two recommended contraceptive methods including one highly effective plus one barrier unless committed abstinence; continue during and 24 months after the last dose. Amenorrhoea is not evidence of infertility.
No breastfeeding during treatment or 24 months after the final dose.
Men: condom with spermicide if available, even after vasectomy, during treatment and 2 months after the final dose; no semen donation during treatment or 2 months after. Report partner pregnancy.
No blood donation during treatment or 24 months after the final dose.
Discuss fertility preservation before treatment; female fertility impairment/amenorrhoea can occur and reversibility is uncertain.
Record the actual final dose date so post-treatment pregnancy/donation precautions can be followed.
Review poor intake, taste change, cramps, weight loss and hydration; supportive measures are individual, not a fixed prophylactic prescription.

baseline: Pregnancy Prevention Programme assessment and registration for male and female patients
WCBP: medically supervised negative pregnancy test within 7 days before initiation; minimum assay sensitivity 25 mIU/mL as per local availability
during: FBC, renal and liver profile every 4 weeks
WCBP: medically supervised pregnancy test monthly, including amenorrhoea
Review benefit, tolerance, weight/appetite, cramps, medicines and skin symptoms regularly
Severe renal impairment: careful adverse-reaction monitoring
monitoring.disease_monitoring: Disease examination, imaging and any additional tests follow the individual consultant plan. No universal imaging interval or tumour-marker panel is specified.
monitoring.not_routine: No mandatory routine CPK interval or CPK dose-modification threshold is specified by the reviewed NCCP/EMA sources. Muscle symptoms or CK elevation require clinical assessment.
